## Why we are asking

We have turned what you told us in September into three different screen designs for the same job: checking a device in, diagnosing and repairing it, and keeping parts in stock. Before we choose one and build it, we need your view on which design suits your staff and your stores, and your answers to a few business rules we cannot decide for you. Your answers decide what we build next, so there are no wrong ones, and “not sure” is a useful answer. The packet takes about 30 minutes. One of us can walk through it with you in person, or you can write your answers in the boxes and send it back. Section 3 has the two questions we most need answered before we can finish the design.

| Section | What we ask | Time |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Three screen designs | Rate each design, then choose one and tell us what to keep from the others | 15 min |
| 2. Your staff and stores | Who uses the screens, where, and what would make them easier to use | 5 min |
| 3. Decisions we need from you | Business rules only you can set; two are blocking | 5 min |
| 4. Equipment and support | What you have today and who looks after the system after December 9 | 3 min |
| 5. What we have on record | Check that we have understood you correctly | 2 min |

## 1. Three screen designs

All three designs do the same work and follow the rules you confirmed. They differ in how the screens are laid out and how staff move through a job. The screens use made-up sample customers and parts. Please look at each one as if you were standing at the counter or sitting at the repair bench.

## 2. Your staff and stores

These answers tell us whether the design works for the people who will use it every day, including anyone who finds small text, colours or fast-moving screens hard to use.

4. Who will use the system at each store (how many front desk staff, technicians and managers), and how comfortable are they with computers?

5. Would any staff member find it easier with larger text, a language other than English, or less reliance on colour? Is there anything else that makes screens hard for someone on your team to use?

6. Where will each screen be used: at the counter, at the repair bench, or both? Standing or sitting, in bright light, with busy or dirty hands?

7. At the bench, would technicians rather use a shared computer, a tablet or a phone?

8. Do you want a printed claim ticket for the customer and a tag on each device? Do you print anything today?  (FR03)

9. On a busy day, how long should checking in a device take at most?

## 3. Decisions we need from you

These are business rules, not design choices, so we will not guess. The first two hold up the design; the rest change smaller parts of the screens.

### Needed before we finish the design

10. When a repair is finished, should staff click a button to send the customer’s email, or should it go automatically when the job is marked Ready for Pickup?  (FR12)

11. You approve every purchase order. Is there an amount below which a Manager can approve alone, or a quicker path for urgent parts when you cannot be reached?  (FR10)

### Needed before we build

12. Should the customer sign when they collect their device?  (FR08)

13. How do you decide which technician is available for an appointment, and who may move an appointment?  (FR01)

14. If a device cannot be repaired and goes back to the customer, do you charge a diagnostic fee? How much?  (FR05)

15. Who decides the reorder point for each part (the stock level that triggers reordering)?  (FR10)

16. What does the front desk write down when a device comes in today? Should the system keep a customer’s device passcode, or never store it?  (UC-01)

## 4. Equipment and support

We know of one laptop and a card machine. Before we recommend how the system is obtained and what it runs on, we need a fuller picture. Any cost we show you later will be an estimate based on these answers.

17. What computers, tablets, phones and printers are at each store today, and how old are they?

18. Is the internet at both stores reliable? How often does it go down?

19. Have you used or looked at any ready-made repair-shop software? What did you like or dislike about it?

20. Would you prefer a ready-made product with a monthly fee, if it covered most of your needs, or a system built for your shop? Is there a monthly or one-time amount you would not go above?

21. After we hand over on December 9, who will look after the system: add staff accounts, fix problems and keep the data safe?

## 5. What we have on record

Please tick each line that is still correct and correct any that are not. Items 1–7 are what you confirmed in September. Items 8–12 are decisions our team made since then that you have not yet seen.
